pages.lesson:
LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 GENDER NEUTRAL LANGUAGE

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How can one avoid gender bias in communication?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify gender biased words and phrases in oral and written texts
2. use gender neutral words and phrases in sentences

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language

Teach
• Focus skill: identify gender biased words and phrases in oral and written texts.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can one avoid gender bias in communication?
2. Which words demonstrate gender sensitivity in communication?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
